prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map shows an outdoor dirt and grass clearing with a car trunk on the right, two boulders, climbing gear on the ground, a person in a grey t-shirt very close (~0.3–0.8 m, within arm's reach of the camera wearer), and a second person in a plaid shirt and grey shorts standing ~2–3 m away (~2–3 m from the person in grey). In Frame 1, the person in grey is directly in front of the camera wearer and occludes most of the background, then shifts to the bottom-right foreground in Frames 2–4 as the camera wearer turns left toward the standing person (whose upper torso and head are cropped out in Frames 2–3), before the camera wearer turns right in Frame 5 to face the person in grey leaning into the open car trunk (~0.5–1.2 m away). In Frames 2–4, backpacks, ropes, a white/blue box, and two boulders (one left with clothing draped on it, one right with a light-blue towel) lie on the ground below eye level at ~1.5–3 m, within or just beyond the standing person's reach while the open trunk stays within reach of both the camera wearer and the person in grey. The depth map clearly separates the foreground shoulder/back of the person in grey and the distinct 3D mounds of the boulders and gear piles from the sloped ground plane, which blend together in texture in the RGB image. However, it provides no facial or gaze detail to tell whether anyone looks at the camera wearer, and it merges fine objects like thin climbing ropes into the ground while flattening the interior cavity of the open car trunk in Frame 5.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map isolates discrete regions in only four of the five frames, failing to detect anything in Frame 1 despite the person in the grey shirt filling the center foreground at ~0.3–0.5 m. In Frames 2–4, it segments the person in the plaid shirt standing ~2–3 m ahead (shifting from upper-center to the far left edge as the camera wearer turns right), and in Frame 5 it segments the person in the grey shirt (~0.5 m ahead, facing away into the trunk) as a large pink mask in the center foreground. The map captures how the standing person's head and shoulders are cut off by the top frame edge in Frames 2–3 before their full side profile appears in Frame 4, and it outlines a small backpack mask (~2 m away, below and to the right of the standing person's feet) in Frame 2 where overlapping gear is visually cluttered in RGB. However, the segmentation map is highly unreliable across the scene: it completely misses the foreground person's shoulder in Frames 2–3, most of the backpacks and climbing gear on the ground, and the car trunk in Frame 5. Furthermore, it severely misclassifies the left boulder with draped clothes in Frame 3 as a 'horse' (~2.5 m away, left of the standing person) and mislabels both the right boulder with a towel (~2 m away) and the open car trunk/person on the right (~0.5–1.5 m away) in Frame 4 as another 'person' and a 'motorcycle'.
descriptions.pose: The pose map is completely blank in Frames 1, 2, 3, and 5, detecting a yellow body skeleton only in Frame 4 for the person in the plaid shirt standing near the left edge at ~2.5–3 m from the camera wearer. In Frame 4, the skeleton's torso, legs, head keypoints, and bent arms show that this person is standing upright above the sloped ground, turned slightly rightward in three-quarter profile, and looking downward toward the hands holding climbing gear at chest level rather than toward the camera wearer. The pose keypoints clarify the exact joint articulation of the person's bent elbows and knees amidst the busy plaid pattern and background grass in the RGB frame, showing their hands positioned right in front of their chest within their own immediate reach while their feet stand just behind and left of the gear pile (~0.5 m from the ropes and boxes). However, the map is unreliable whenever bodies are heavily cropped or seen from behind at close range: it completely misses the standing person in Frames 2–3 where their head and upper torso are out of view above the top frame boundary, and it fails to detect the person in the grey shirt at ~0.3–0.8 m in Frames 1–5 (who faces away into the car trunk within the camera wearer's arm's reach). Additionally, no magenta hand skeletons are detected in any frame, leaving fine hand poses on the held gear in Frames 3–4 and inside the trunk in Frame 5 unrepresented.
